claims.text: Template Method pattern: a base-class method (the template method) fixes the order of the steps and leaves one or more of them abstract for subclasses to fill in.
claims.source_hint: glossary template-method-pattern; GoF book, Template Method pattern

claims.text: At stage-1 NotifierBase (abstract, implements INotifier) has a private List<string> sent exposed as IReadOnlyList<string> Sent; Send(orderId, subject) calls Format, then sent.Add(message), then Console.WriteLine(message); Format is protected abstract.

At stage-1 EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier (sealed, derive from NotifierBase) override only Format, returning "email about order {orderId}: {subject}" / "sms about order ..."; they declare no Send, list or console call.
Calling Send on an EmailNotifier runs the Send inherited from NotifierBase; inside it, the call to the abstract Format runs the override of the object's actual class (EmailNotifier).
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: inheritance; abstract and override (virtual method invocation)

claims.text: A private field of a base class is not accessible from derived classes; a protected member is accessible only within its class and derived classes, so outside code cannot call Format directly.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: access modifiers (private, protected)

claims.text: A non-abstract class that derives from an abstract class must override every abstract member (else a compile error), so each notifier has to supply Format.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: abstract keyword (non-abstract class derived from abstract class must implement all inherited abstract members)

claims.text: Declaring 'public override void Send(...)' in a NotifierBase subclass fails to compile with error CS0506 because NotifierBase.Send is not virtual, abstract or override.
claims.source_hint: C# compiler error CS0506; verified locally on stage-1 archive (.NET SDK 10.0)

claims.text: A C# class can derive from only one base class (single inheritance of classes).
INotifier (stage-1 samples) declares only void Send(int orderId, string subject); NotifierBase implements it with its Send, so a caller that knows only INotifier gets the fixed order.

At stage-1 ShippingFee is abstract with only abstract ForOrder(int totalVnd); no base-class method calls ForOrder. At stage-2 CheckoutTotal takes a ShippingFee through its constructor (used as a strategy).

Try it at stage-1: PushNotifier : NotifierBase (Format only) plus a test asserting the single Sent entry is "push about order 42: paid"; dotnet test ... --filter PushNotifierTests prints Passed!, 0 failed, 1 passed. SamplesTests.cs has using DonHang.Samples.Oop.
claims.source_hint: run on stage-1 archive (verified locally with .NET SDK 10.0); samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests/SamplesTests.cs:2

claims.text: Template Method varies a step through inheritance, fixed when the subclass is written; Strategy varies it through an object handed in, which can be chosen while the program runs.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; GoF book, Template Method vs Strategy

claims.text: With single inheritance, two independently varying steps need a subclass per combination (2 wordings x 2 destinations = 4; a third wording adds 2); handing in one object per step avoids that. Template Method fits when one step varies.

In C# a subclass can override only a base-class method marked as open to it (abstract, as Format is; methods are non-virtual by default); NotifierBase.Send has no such mark, so a subclass cannot override it (CS0506).
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: virtual keyword ('By default, methods are non-virtual. You can't override a non-virtual method.'); abstract; CS0506
